guidance.heading: Fiscal Year 2027 Outlook
section: The Company’s outlook for fiscal year 2027 with regard to revenue, net income, Adjusted net income, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA margin is as follows:
•Revenue in the range of $4.175 billion to $4.275 billion
•Net income in the range of $170.9 million to $180.8 million
•Adjusted net income(1) in the range of $174.6 million to $185.4 million
•Adjusted EBITDA(1) in the range of $585.0 million to $620.0 million
•Adjusted EBITDA margin(1) in the range of 14.0% to 14.5%

Ned N. Fleming, III, the Company’s Executive Chairman, stated, “This year once again showed the strength of CPI’s differentiated business model. Our industry remains highly fragmented, and as many family-owned businesses across the Sunbelt navigate generational transitions, CPI has become an acquirer of choice for experienced operators who want to preserve their legacy and grow their businesses. The ten acquisitions we have completed since the start of fiscal 2026 are a testament to how repeatable this approach has become. Looking ahead, the long-term drivers of demand in our markets, including aging infrastructure, population growth and rising traffic volumes, remain firmly intact, and our states and municipalities continue to show a strong commitment to roadway investment. With a strong balance sheet and a disciplined leadership team, the Board and I remain highly confident in CPI’s ability to expand its footprint, increase its scale and enhance shareholder value.”

desk.headline: Record Q4 revenue up 22% to $1.10bn, slightly above estimates; EPS $1.00 just short as rain and diesel hit margins; FY27 outlook reiterated

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP (no quarterly adjusted EPS given)

results: Q4 revenue rose 22% to a record $1.10bn, but net income was flat at $56.2m and diluted EPS slipped to $1.00 from $1.02.
Results were in line with the preliminary ranges the company gave in early November.
Full year: revenue up 31% to $3.67bn (7% organic, the rest from seven acquisitions); net income up 40% to $142.1m.
Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 14.2% from 15.1%; Q4 gross margin dropped to 15.5% from 17.7%.
Backlog of $3.29bn, up from $3.03bn a year earlier; three more acquisitions after year-end added $65m.

guidance.summary: Fiscal 2027 outlook, first given in early November, was reiterated: about 15% growth in revenue and adjusted EBITDA, with margins flat to slightly up.

points: Wet weather in July and August was the biggest drag on Q4 margins, with diesel prices up about 40% since August adding to it.
Higher diesel costs are being passed through in new pricing, which management expects to lift margins in the second half of FY27.
Lower-margin backlog inherited with acquisitions should be replaced by better work over the coming year.
About 6–8% organic growth is expected in FY27; the first half should bring roughly 40–42% of yearly revenue.
Net leverage was 3.24x, with a goal of about 2.5x; deal talks with sellers continue. ROAD 2030 targets were repeated.
call.source: Call coverage: MarketBeat via Yahoo Finance and Investing.com, 19 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)
